terms.gloss: napkin, tied round the neck as a bib
evidence: Petr. 32.2: circā onerātās veste cervīcēs lāticlāviam immīserat mappam (Lewis & Short, s.v. immittō)
terms.comment: Latin has no word of its own for a bib. Trimalchio puts a napkin round his neck (Petr. 32.2), and Vives’s diners fit theirs to their shoulders or chests (Exercitatio 362, via Morgan–Owens). The same word as the napkin.
Levi–Bini’s word for a bib, and Vives’s for the napkin; in the house it is the hand towel (Jack, 29 October 2026).

phrases.latin: Mappam collō tuō circumdabō, nē vestem maculēs.
phrases.english: I’ll put your bib on, so you don’t get your clothes dirty.

sources: Lewis & Short: mappa · Lewis & Short: mappula · Lewis & Short: mantele · Lewis & Short: immitto
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. table linen: napkin. Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 9, s.v. bavaglio. Traupman has no word.
